Living Well / Free resources

Useful tools & everyday skills

A useful way in

Choose one place to begin.

Free core tools and readable guides for notes, documents, sources, audio, maps, and small practical tasks.

Start with a task rather than a tool collection. A document that opens reliably, a note you can find again, or a clear recording may be all you need. The selections here offer free core functions or free instructions, with installation, optional services, and practical limits identified.

Start with: LibreOffice. Read the system requirements and try a non-sensitive document from an official download.

Documents and spreadsheets · Free core app

LibreOffice

The Document Foundation

A full document toolkit for readers who need ordinary office tasks without a recurring software subscription.

Begin here: Read the system requirements and try a non-sensitive document from an official download.

Access: Free, open-source desktop office suite. Installation is required; optional support services are separate.

Perspective: Official open-source software

Notes and organization · Free core app

Joplin

Joplin project

A possible home for notes that need to remain understandable and portable, without building a complicated personal dashboard.

Begin here: Read the app and synchronization options, then try one small notebook.

Access: The note-taking apps are free and open source. Joplin Cloud and some services are paid options.

Perspective: Official software documentation

Explore Joplin

Context & source

Sync, backup, and encryption choices need deliberate setup; free software is not a blanket privacy guarantee.

Sources and reading · Free core app

Zotero

Corporation for Digital Scholarship

A practical way to keep the source behind an interesting idea so it can be found and checked again.

Begin here: Save one public article and inspect its title, author, and link for accuracy.

Access: The core research application is free. Additional hosted file storage is an optional paid service.

Perspective: Official research software

Explore Zotero

Context & source

Automatically captured metadata needs checking; the tool does not establish that a source is reliable.

Audio recording and editing · Free core app

Audacity

Audacity project

A useful option for making a clear recording or editing an agreed conversation without building a full production setup.

Begin here: Use the official download and manual, then test a short recording of your own voice.

Access: The core audio editor is free and open source. Installation is required; additional services have separate terms.

Perspective: Official audio software

Maps and local knowledge · Free to browse

OpenStreetMap

OpenStreetMap contributors and Foundation

An example of shared knowledge made useful through technology, with ordinary places and paths as a starting point.

Begin here: Explore a familiar area and compare the map with information you can independently verify.

Access: The map is free to browse. An account is needed to contribute edits; other map services set their own terms.

Perspective: Community-maintained map data

Practical instructions · Free to browse

iFixit repair guides

iFixit and its contributors

A reminder that a useful technology decision can involve understanding and maintaining something rather than replacing it.

Begin here: Browse a low-risk clothing or household guide and read every step before deciding whether to attempt it.

Access: The step-by-step guides are free to read. Tools, parts, and optional services are not necessarily free.

Perspective: Repair education from a commercial provider

Keep the context

Take what is useful, thoughtfully.

Choose official download routes and review the current requirements before installing anything. Keep backups when changing a working process, and test a non-sensitive example first. A free application can offer paid storage or services; a free repair guide does not make equipment free or a hazardous repair safe to attempt.

Selections are based on public source review, not a claim that Nolan uses every resource or belongs to the organizations listed.
